purpose: Record the Batanes coral-reef fish assessment summarized in the 2024 UP Marine Science Institute report without deriving species rows, site occurrences, or map coordinates from aggregate metrics and figures.

source.title: The West Philippine Sea: State of the Coasts — Chapter 2.1: Batanes
source.publication: The West Philippine Sea: State of the Coasts, pp. 103-108; University of the Philippines Marine Science Institute, 2024; UP MSI Contribution No. 1597
source.citation: Heyres, L. J., Cabasan, J. P., Sabban, F. B., Luciano, R. M., Valiño, D. A., & Arceo, H. O. (2024). Batanes. In H. O. Arceo, M. J. P. Velos, M. A. C. Nuñez, & P. M. Aliño (Eds.), The West Philippine Sea: State of the Coasts (pp. 103-108). University of the Philippines Marine Science Institute. ISBN 978-621-8152-14-4.

studyScope.setting: Coral-reef fish assemblage assessment; marine evidence only.
studyScope.project: CARE-CaDRES Updating Coral Reef Baseline Data: West Philippine Sea Project, funded by DENR-BMB.
studyScope.administrativeCoverage: Eight assessment stations spread across five Batanes municipalities.
studyScope.stationNote: The report states that an asterisk marks stations with fewer than three replicate transects.
studyScope.localityPrecision: The chapter names stations and shows them on figures but provides no coordinate table or verified station-to-coordinate crosswalk. Do not georeference points from the illustrative map.

reportedFindings.aggregateSpeciesRichness: The chapter reports 161 coral-reef fish species from 28 families and subfamilies observed in Batanes during the assessment.
reportedFindings.meanSpeciesRichness: 35 species per 500 m2 across stations; reported station values range from 20 at Nakanmuan to 45 at Basco.
reportedFindings.speciesListStatus: The reviewed chapter does not provide the complete 161-name checklist or a species-by-station matrix.
reportedFindings.evidenceLevel: Aggregate survey summary only. The reported species total does not identify which species occurred at any particular station and is not a current-range, catchability, diet, legal, safety, or conservation-status statement.

qualityAndReuseLimits: This is marine coral-reef evidence and does not add freshwater evidence for Batanes lakes, rivers, reservoirs, or wetlands.
The 161-species total is an aggregate result, not a complete accessible checklist; do not create 161 taxa rows, station occurrence rows, or a complete provincial checklist from it.
The figures show station labels and summary categories, not specimen-level records or exact station coordinates; no geometry or map pins were derived.

The report's reproduction permission allows copying or adaptation only when distributed free and credited to the authors or original source. This is not a blanket CC license. No figures, maps, tables, or full species list were copied or adapted; review third-party credits and intended use before any future reuse.
The report summarizes a 2017 assessment; its biomass and density findings are historical survey metrics and are not current stock estimates.
nextAction: Search for a public CARE-CaDRES field checklist, station metadata, or voucher-linked dataset that resolves individual fish names and sampling sites. Keep this aggregate Batanes reef assessment research-only and continue the separate freshwater source queue.
